result:
No Revisit dates have passed. The next one is the bake-to-order decision on 2 December.

**You're already growing. Before adding customers, check you have room for them on Saturdays.** You got 15 paid signups in October, so the paid-from-week-one model works. Saturday delivery slots are your real limit (that's what the free-box trial ran into). Before pushing harder, work out how many more boxes you can bake and deliver on a Saturday. That number is your real target.

Here's what I'd do, in order:

1. **Subscriber referrals.** This is your strongest lever, and it's the one discarded idea the ledger allows back in. On 2026-10-06 you dropped "50% off the first month" because you expected the same low conversion as the free box. The reopen condition was "test it with a referral from an existing subscriber." So run that test: a subscriber invites a friend, the friend gets 50% off their first month, and the subscriber gets something cheap to you, like a pastry in their next box. Friends of happy subscribers are likely to stay much longer than strangers chasing a free box. Run it for 6–8 weeks and compare conversion.

2. **Christmas gift boxes, starting now.** Sell paid 4-week and 8-week gift subscriptions, with a printed card to put under the tree. The buyer pays full price, so it doesn't conflict with the no-free-trial decision. The recipient tries the bread at no cost to you, and some will renew.

3. **Target the neighbours of your current subscribers.** Your 3 km radius is an advantage here. When you deliver, put a card through 5–10 nearby doors saying something like "Your neighbour gets warm sourdough from us every Saturday" with a QR code. You're already on that street, so it costs no extra delivery time. Your cargo bike is also an advert on every round, so make sure the branding and QR code are visible on it.

4. **Turn shop customers into subscribers.** Put a QR code on every bag and by the till, and have one sentence ready at the counter about the Saturday box. A small tasting plate of the box bread costs very little and doesn't use any Saturday slots, which is why the free box failed.

5. **Local partners.** A cheese shop, wine shop or greengrocer within 3 km could share flyers or offer a joint box. Also post in neighbourhood WhatsApp or Facebook groups and school parent groups. These cost almost nothing.

6. **Reduce cancellations.** If people cancel because they're away, offer a "pause" option instead of a cancel button. Every subscriber you keep is one fewer you have to find.

For €300 a month: about €100 on printing (door cards, bag inserts, gift cards), €100 on referral rewards, and €100 on a small boosted local social post for the gift boxes in December.

I've left out delivery apps and courier partners (discarded 2026-08-18) and the free first box (discarded 2026-10-06). None of their reopen conditions has been met: you have one shop, about 140 subscribers, and 15 signups a month.

If you go ahead with the referral test or the gift boxes, tell me and I'll log it in the ledger.
